links.outcome: Output variability across 3 identical repeated runs of ethics questions
links.effect: GPT-4o varied on 27/130 (21%) general vs 3/70 (4%) orthopedic questions (P=.002); Claude varied on 16/130 (12%) vs 3/70 (4%) (P=.06).
links.quote: GPT-4o provided different responses to identically worded trials for 27 (21%) of 130 general questions and 3 (4%) of 70 orthopedic questions (P=.002), while Claude did not have a significant difference in variability between these 2 groups (general: 16/130, 12% vs orthopedic: 3/70, 4%; P=.06).

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance and variability of GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet on medical ethics multiple-choice questions from medical student and orthopedic resident question banks, comparing AI performance to human benchmarks without evaluating a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
